hints.title: Modulo Remainder Maximum Sum Obstacle
hints.text: Selecting elements from nums to maximize total sum such that sum % 3 == 0 requires tracking the best achievable sums across all three possible remainders. How can updating remainder states per number accumulate the maximum sum?

hints.title: Modulo Three State Triple Invariant
hints.text: Adding number x to a sum with remainder r transitions to remainder (r + x) % 3. Keeping the maximum sum for remainders 0, 1, and 2 guarantees optimal transitions.

hints.title: Three-Element Array Transition Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an array of size 3 to [0, -infinity, -infinity]. For each number x, create a copy of the current three values. For each remainder r from 0 to 2, update nxt[(r + x) % 3] to max(nxt[(r + x) % 3], dp[r] + x). Replace dp with nxt. Return dp[0].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Single pass over nums updating a 3-element remainder array.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all 2^N subsets takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Array of length 3 takes constant O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Tracking three remainder states (mod 0, mod 1, mod 2) with negative infinity initializers.
